scope_note: Outcome labels apply only to the named product, operator and domain scope. Related tokens, successor operators, local-market sites and separately regulated venues are excluded unless expressly included.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers the international polymarket.com peer-to-peer prediction market. It excludes the independently operated, CFTC-regulated Polymarket US venue operated by QCX LLC and does not treat QCX's DCM designation as regulation of the international platform.

sources.title: Popular Predictions & Real-Time Odds
sources.notes: Current product, operator, market model, active-market and international-versus-US scope source.

sources.title: CFTC Orders Event-Based Binary Options Markets Operator to Pay $1.4 Million Penalty
sources.notes: Official historical enforcement and wind-down order.

sources.title: Designated Contract Markets filing 49571
sources.notes: Official designation record for QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US; scope counterevidence, not an international-platform licence.

claims.evidence_locator: Footer identifies Adventure One QSS Inc. and expressly says the international platform operates independently from CFTC-regulated Polymarket US.
claims.analyst_note: Prevents importing the US DCM status into the international case.

claims.evidence_locator: Current page lists active markets across many categories with market-level volume and liquidity.
claims.analyst_note: Market-page figures are dynamic snapshots, not audited company revenue.

claims.evidence_locator: CFTC ordered Blockratize d/b/a Polymarket to pay $1.4 million, wind down noncompliant markets and cease violations.
claims.analyst_note: Historical enforcement is retained beside the later operating success.

claims.evidence_locator: CFTC record lists QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US as a designated DCM.
claims.analyst_note: This supports a separate US regulatory path, not an international-platform licence claim.

licences.notes: Explicitly out of product scope; included to prevent false attribution of this designation to polymarket.com.

events.description: CFTC settlement required a civil penalty and wind-down of noncompliant markets.

outcome.label: successful
outcome.summary: The international Polymarket venue is active at material market-level scale after surviving a 2022 US enforcement reset. Success here means durable product activity and category leadership, not proven profitability or blanket regulatory approval.

why.summary: A peer-to-peer exchange model, broad event catalogue and continuously visible odds created an information product as well as a wagering venue. The evidence supports product breadth and activity, but not a controlled causal decomposition.

strategic_choices.decision: Operate a peer-to-peer prediction exchange rather than take the house side of each wager.
strategic_choices.consequence: The venue can aggregate trader beliefs across many event types, while liquidity and resolution integrity become central dependencies.

strategic_choices.decision: Comply with the 2022 CFTC order and pursue a separate regulated US venue.
strategic_choices.consequence: The structure preserved an international product while separating the later US DCM; the two regulatory scopes must not be conflated.

counterfactual.summary: Without the 2022 compliance reset and a legally separate US route, US re-entry would likely have remained blocked. This is an inference, not a finding in the designation record.

watch.signal: International market volume and liquidity under stable definitions.
watch.implication: Sustained depth supports durable exchange utility; concentration or sharp decay would weaken the success classification.

watch.signal: Changes to the international-versus-US entity and regulatory disclosures.
watch.implication: A structure change could alter legal availability without implying the same status across both venues.

unknowns: What are audited international revenue, profitability and liabilities?
How much displayed volume is incentive-driven, wash-like or concentrated?
What is the final ownership and intercompany relationship between the current international operator and QCX?

synthesis.present_situation: The international venue is active with broad, liquid event markets and a clear disclosure that it is separate from Polymarket US.
synthesis.business_mechanism: Peer-to-peer event shares trade at prices interpreted as probabilities.
synthesis.token_contribution: No official platform token was identified for this case.
synthesis.chain_dependence: The international product uses Polygon settlement infrastructure while curation, access and resolution interfaces remain platform dependencies.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: The 2022 CFTC action is historical; the current US DCM belongs to QCX/Polymarket US and must not be attributed to the international platform.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Breadth, liquidity and information utility plausibly explain durability.
synthesis.counterfactual: A refusal to comply in 2022 likely would have narrowed future US options.
lessons_learned: Regulated sister venues do not automatically regulate an international platform.
Market volume is activity, not company revenue.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers Rollbit's casino and sportsbook operated by Bull Gaming N.V. It excludes treating Rollbit's crypto-futures product as licensed gambling, and it does not classify RLB price performance or Rollbot/Sportsbot NFT investment returns as casino success.
case.token_utility: Buy-and-burn, lottery, rakeback and product-discount utilities described by Rollbit.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: The reviewed 2023 operator materials describe revenue-funded purchases and some NFT staking distributions; they do not establish an unconditional holder claim on audited profit.

sources.title: Rollbit Terms and Conditions
sources.notes: Current operator, licence claim, account and restriction source.

sources.title: RLB Utility Guide
sources.notes: Operator-reported token utility and buy-and-burn metrics; explicitly calls the inputs revenue, not profit.

sources.title: RLB Burn Schedule and History
sources.notes: Historical RLB launch, supply, burns and Solana-to-Ethereum migration source.

sources.title: Rollbit Blog
sources.notes: Current 2026 product and promotion activity; not audited economic evidence.

claims.evidence_locator: Terms identify Bull Gaming N.V. and state the gambling licence claimed for Rollbit.
claims.analyst_note: The same terms distinguish non-gambling crypto trading from regulated gambling activity.

claims.evidence_locator: The operator blog contains current July 2026 casino promotions and community events.
claims.analyst_note: Current publishing supports operational continuity, not profitability.

claims.evidence_locator: Guide reports 33,688,709 RLB bought for $5,538,265.59 after the August 8, 2023 launch, with 90% burned and 10% distributed to Rollbot stakers.
claims.analyst_note: Operator-reported and historical; the page says revenue, not profit.

claims.evidence_locator: Rollbit reports RLB launched on Solana on November 10, 2021 with five billion initial supply and later migrated to Ethereum.
claims.analyst_note: Historical token facts do not establish current supply or token-holder returns.

events.description: Rollbit reports that RLB launched on Solana.
Rollbit reports that RLB migrated from Solana to Ethereum.

outcome.label: successful
outcome.summary: Rollbit remains an active crypto casino and sportsbook with a long-running RLB utility loop. Success is medium-confidence because current operation is visible, while audited revenue, profit, liabilities and user counts remain unavailable.

why.summary: A bundled casino/sportsbook, frequent promotions and token-linked rewards plausibly reinforce retention. Public evidence establishes the product design and continuity but cannot isolate which component drives economics.

strategic_choices.decision: Tie RLB purchases and burns to reported casino, sportsbook and futures revenue inputs.
strategic_choices.consequence: The mechanism created visible token demand and product cross-linkage, but operator-defined revenue is not audited profit and the futures component is outside the gambling-licence conclusion.

strategic_choices.decision: Bundle casino, sportsbook and crypto-native rewards under a custodial account.
strategic_choices.consequence: The bundle expands cross-sell opportunities while concentrating custody, KYC and jurisdiction risk at the operator.

counterfactual.summary: Without the RLB rewards and burn loop, Rollbit likely would have had less crypto-native differentiation. The evidence does not quantify incremental retention or profit from the token.

watch.signal: Current operator and licence disclosures in Rollbit terms.
watch.implication: A change may alter legal availability without establishing product failure.

watch.signal: RLB burn cadence and the revenue-input definitions.
watch.implication: Sustained transparent purchases support token-loop durability; unexplained pauses weaken it.

unknowns: What are audited casino and sportsbook GGR, profit and player liabilities?
How many unique active bettors use each product?
What is the current RLB supply and how much token demand is organic rather than operator-funded?

synthesis.present_situation: Rollbit's casino and sportsbook remain active with current publishing and a continuing RLB narrative.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A custodial crypto casino and sportsbook uses promotions and token-linked rewards for acquisition and retention.
synthesis.token_contribution: RLB supports burns, lottery, rakeback and discounts; historical operator metrics do not prove current profitability.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Crypto rails and Ethereum RLB are important, while wagers and balances are primarily operator-ledger activity.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: Gambling and crypto-futures scope must be separated; the reviewed operator terms do not make futures a licensed gambling product.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Bundle breadth and token-linked rewards plausibly support durability.
synthesis.counterfactual: Removing the token loop likely reduces differentiation, but its marginal contribution is unknown.

outlook.scope_guard: crypto futures excluded from gambling-licence conclusion

lessons_learned: Revenue-funded token purchases are not profit.
Casino success does not establish token or NFT investment success.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers Augur v2's live Moon Fork and the Lituus Foundation-coordinated Augur Lituus oracle reboot. It excludes Dark Florist as an independent product and does not classify REP token price performance as protocol recovery.
case.token_utility: Dispute staking and migration between Augur universes.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: No current unconditional protocol-revenue right was established in the reviewed evidence.

sources.title: Augur Is Testing Its Past and Building Its Future
sources.notes: Current fork, implementation, governance, scope and migration-deadline source.

sources.title: Q1 2026 Progress Report
sources.notes: Migration, ChainSafe implementation and public-development corroboration.

sources.title: Phase 2: The Fork Migration
sources.notes: One-way REP migration and unmigrated-token risk source.

claims.evidence_locator: Augur reports its first live fork, Lituus implementation by ChainSafe and a separately funded Dark Florist effort after long stretches out of the news.
claims.analyst_note: Recovery refers to resumed protocol work, not restored consumer-market adoption.

claims.evidence_locator: Article reports roughly 200,000 REP contributed to fund the first live fork triggered April 8, 2026.
claims.analyst_note: REP committed to a mechanism test is not trading volume, users or revenue.

claims.evidence_locator: Foundation describes one-way migration and warns unmigrated REP may be left outside the active system and lose economic value.
claims.analyst_note: A migration risk disclosure, not a token-price forecast.

claims.evidence_locator: Progress report describes ChainSafe partnership and public implementation work.
claims.analyst_note: Implementation progress does not equal audited production readiness.

events.description: Augur's first live fork was triggered around the Artemis II market.

outcome.label: recovering
outcome.summary: Augur has resumed public, technically concrete work after long quiet periods: a first live v2 fork is running and ChainSafe is implementing the redesigned Lituus oracle. Recovery is not yet equivalent to renewed consumer adoption.

why.summary: The reboot narrows the thesis from a full prediction-market destination toward reusable resolution infrastructure, while testing the original fork mechanism under live incentives. Public implementation and a specialist partner make the recovery more than a whitepaper-only announcement.

strategic_choices.decision: Trigger and observe the original v2 fork mechanism in public.
strategic_choices.consequence: The project gains real behavioral evidence, but REP holders face a one-way migration decision and potential loss on unmigrated tokens.

strategic_choices.decision: Reframe Lituus as resolution infrastructure beneath multiple applications and engage ChainSafe to implement it.
strategic_choices.consequence: The addressable customer moves beyond Augur's own frontend, while production readiness still depends on implementation, audit and integrations.

counterfactual.summary: An earlier focus on oracle infrastructure and simpler distribution might have reduced the long adoption gap, but the reviewed sources do not provide comparative adoption data.

watch.signal: REP migration participation after the August 1, 2026 deadline.
watch.implication: Broad migration would support governance continuity; low participation would expose a weak active base.

watch.signal: Public Lituus implementation, audits and external integrations.
watch.implication: Shipped, reviewed code and customers would move the case from recovery toward success.

unknowns: What share of REP migrates before the deadline?
How many active users and how much market volume remain on Augur v2?
What is the Foundation's funding runway and when will Lituus receive an independent audit?
Will any external prediction market integrate Lituus?

synthesis.present_situation: A live fork and public Lituus implementation support a recovery classification, not a claim of restored mass adoption.
synthesis.business_mechanism: Augur uses economically secured decentralized dispute resolution for prediction outcomes.
synthesis.token_contribution: REP secures disputes and must migrate into a fork universe; token price is outside the recovery conclusion.
synthesis.chain_dependence: The live mechanism and migration execute on Ethereum.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: The dominant near-term risks are technical, governance and migration participation; this review did not establish a current gambling-licence position.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Narrower infrastructure positioning and public implementation may correct the original distribution problem.
synthesis.counterfactual: Earlier infrastructure focus might have improved distribution, but evidence is insufficient to quantify it.
lessons_learned: A live mechanism test is stronger than a roadmap.
Technical recovery must not be confused with user or revenue recovery.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers the purported ZKasino gambling platform and its 2024 bridge-deposit scheme. It does not attribute liability to unrelated projects, exchanges or persons beyond what the Dutch FIOD publicly alleged, and it does not treat suspicion as conviction.
case.token_utility: Promised replacement/vesting token associated with deposited assets; final launch and redemption status were not established.
case.token_fee_revenue_rights: No verified holder revenue right was established.

sources.title: More than 11 million euros seized and man arrested in investigation into gambling platform scam
sources.publisher: FIOD Fiscal Information and Investigation Service
sources.notes: Dutch investigative authority source; allegations and suspicion are not a conviction.

sources.title: FIOD Annual Report 2024
sources.publisher: FIOD Fiscal Information and Investigation Service
sources.notes: Annual-report corroboration of FIOD's 2024 criminal-investigation activity; not a final judicial disposition.

claims.evidence_locator: FIOD says victims worldwide invested more than $30 million in cryptocurrency in the alleged platform.
claims.analyst_note: Reported deposited/invested value, not audited revenue or final adjudicated loss.

claims.evidence_locator: FIOD says investors were led to expect return within 30 days, which did not happen, and the contract design suggested return was not intended.
claims.analyst_note: Supports platform failure and suspected rug-pull mechanics; not a conviction.

claims.evidence_locator: FIOD reports a 26-year-old arrested on suspicion of fraud, embezzlement and money laundering and more than €11.4 million in assets seized.
claims.analyst_note: Arrest and seizure are investigative actions, not proof of guilt.

events.description: FIOD arrested a suspect and reported asset seizures in the ZKasino investigation.

outcome.label: failed
outcome.summary: ZKasino failed as a credible gambling-platform launch: the Dutch FIOD describes more than $30 million deposited by victims, an unfulfilled 30-day return promise and a contract design suggesting return was not intended. Criminal allegations remain allegations pending final disposition.

why.summary: The product proposition was subordinated to a deposit mechanism that did not preserve the promised redemption path. No reviewed evidence established a durable playable casino, while enforcement evidence documents suspected fraud and asset seizure.

strategic_choices.decision: Solicit crypto through a smart-contract bridge with a promised return window.
strategic_choices.consequence: Users concentrated redemption dependence in contract/controller behavior; the authority says repayment did not occur and contract design suggested it was not intended.

counterfactual.summary: Immutable redemption rights, segregated assets, independent contract audits and milestone escrow could have prevented a controller from changing or obstructing the promised return path. This is a controls inference, not an FIOD conclusion.

watch.implication: Charges, acquittal, conviction or dismissal would refine the legal characterization.

watch.signal: Verified restitution and remaining contract balances.
watch.implication: Recovery data would distinguish gross deposited value from final victim loss.

unknowns: What amount was ultimately returned to depositors?
What is the final criminal-case disposition?
Who controlled the relevant contracts and benefited from transfers?
Was any independently verifiable, playable casino ever delivered?

synthesis.present_situation: No credible active casino was established; the defining record is a Dutch criminal investigation into the deposit scheme.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A purported blockchain-casino launch solicited crypto via a bridge and promised later return.
synthesis.token_contribution: A promised ZKAS substitution did not establish a verified redeemable or revenue-bearing token.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Smart-contract control was central to deposit and restitution risk.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: FIOD allegations are strong authority evidence but are not a conviction; language remains allegation-qualified.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Failure follows the absence of enforceable redemption and a credible delivered product.
synthesis.counterfactual: Segregated assets and immutable redemption could have reduced controller risk.
lessons_learned: Arrest and seizure must not be written as conviction.

case.product_scope_note: This case covers only Small House B.V.'s Curaçao-licensed period and insolvency estate connected to bc.game. It excludes the current international BC.Game brand, any successor/non-Curaçao operator, and any claim that bc.game is currently offline globally.

sources.title: Curaçao Gaming Authority Enforcement Register
sources.notes: Official regulator record listing Small House B.V. licence OGL/2023/118/0060 revoked effective 2024-12-06.

sources.title: Curaçao Court declares bankruptcy for Blockdance and Small House amidst unpaid player claims
sources.notes: Local report of appellate proceedings, operator transfer arguments, player claims and bankruptcy ruling.

sources.title: BC.GAME continues ongoing efforts in strengthening its global compliance strategy
sources.notes: Operator position that it withdrew the Curaçao licence and that international operations and financial health were unaffected; preserved as a conflicting first-party claim.

sources.title: BlockDance and Small House (BC.game) bankruptcy update
sources.publisher: Foundation for Representation of Victims of Online Gaming
sources.notes: Creditor-representative source with an interested-party role; used only for proceeding context.

claims.evidence_locator: Enforcement Register lists Small House B.V., company 164979, OGL/2023/118/0060, revoked effective December 6, 2024.
claims.analyst_note: The official record governs the scoped Curaçao licence status.

claims.evidence_locator: Report says the Court of Appeal overturned earlier rulings and declared Blockdance and Small House bankrupt after finding payment obligations unmet.
claims.analyst_note: Applies only to the named Curaçao entities and period.

claims.evidence_locator: Proceeding report says Blockdance claimed control transferred to Small House after April 30, 2024 and Small House denied assuming existing liabilities.
claims.analyst_note: Reported party positions explain the narrow operator-period scope; they are not an audited asset map.

claims.evidence_locator: BC.Game said it withdrew the Curaçao licence, remained financially healthy and continued international operations.
claims.analyst_note: Preserved as first-party counterevidence to any claim that the global brand ceased; it does not overturn the regulator's revocation record.

claims.evidence_locator: Creditor foundation says it represents a growing claimant group in the BlockDance and Small House bankruptcy proceedings.
claims.analyst_note: Interested-party source; not used alone to establish insolvency.

licences.notes: Revoked effective 2024-12-06. The operator characterized the preceding action as voluntary withdrawal; the regulator register says revoked.

events.description: Curaçao appellate proceedings reportedly resulted in Small House B.V. being declared bankrupt.
CGA enforcement register records the Small House licence as revoked.

outcome.label: failed
outcome.summary: Small House B.V.'s scoped Curaçao BC.Game operator estate failed: the operator was reported bankrupt and its licence is officially listed as revoked. This does not classify the current international BC.Game brand or successor operator as failed.

why.summary: The evidence points to unresolved player-payment obligations, an operator transfer that disputed assumption of prior liabilities, insolvency proceedings and eventual licence revocation. The operator contested the narrative and said international operations were healthy.

strategic_choices.decision: Transfer the bc.game website/software operation from Blockdance to Small House while disputing assumption of legacy player liabilities.
strategic_choices.consequence: The separation became central to creditor litigation and did not prevent the Small House estate from being declared bankrupt.

strategic_choices.decision: Continue the international brand outside Curaçao after the Curaçao operator crisis.
strategic_choices.consequence: Brand continuity became separable from the failure of one legal operator and licence, making entity-level scope essential.

counterfactual.summary: Segregated player funds and an explicit, funded allocation of liabilities during the operator transfer likely would have reduced insolvency and creditor risk. This is an inference; the reviewed evidence is not a complete asset-and-liability audit.

watch.signal: Court or trustee updates on the Small House estate and creditor recoveries.
watch.implication: They will determine whether failure produced partial recovery or a near-total creditor shortfall.
A status change would update the historical licence record but would not automatically identify the current global operator.

watch.signal: Current BC.Game terms naming the international operator and licences.
watch.implication: This is required before making any successor-entity or global-brand conclusion.

unknowns: What is the final creditor recovery from the Small House estate?
What assets and player liabilities moved at each operator transfer?
Who is the current international operator and what is its ownership relationship to Small House?
Will the Curaçao bankruptcy order be modified or rescinded?

synthesis.present_situation: The Small House Curaçao operator estate is insolvent and its licence is revoked; the global brand's current operation is outside scope.
synthesis.business_mechanism: A custodial crypto casino and sportsbook changed legal operators while player liabilities were disputed.
synthesis.token_contribution: No token thesis is evaluated in this operator-estate case.
synthesis.chain_dependence: Crypto deposits increased asset-tracing and custody complexity, but insolvency and licence status are legal-entity facts.
synthesis.risk_legal_posture: Regulator and court evidence supports failure of the named operator; the operator's contrary global-continuity statement remains visible.
synthesis.success_failure_hypotheses: Unresolved liabilities and weak transfer continuity plausibly drove the estate failure.
synthesis.counterfactual: Segregated funds and explicit liability assumption could have reduced creditor risk.
lessons_learned: Brand continuity can outlive a failed legal operator.
Licence withdrawal and regulator-recorded revocation must be presented as conflicting characterizations.
